concerns.text: T013 mandates 'NO fallback to regex' if coverage < 90% or RAM exceeds limits, directly violating Plan.md's 'Model Fallback' section which explicitly permits 'regex-based heuristic distillation' as a mandatory fallback to comply with Constitution Principle VII. This task silently weakens the resource-constrained execution guarantee.

T007c (ResourceWatchdog) enforces a hard exit (code 1) on RAM > 7GB with 'NO fallback', which contradicts T013's requirement to 'attempt the next smaller model' if one fails. The watchdog's strict enforcement prevents the model-fallback logic required by the Plan, creating a semantic conflict that blocks the intended resource-constrained execution strategy.

T021c is scoped to 'Local Mode Only' and explicitly excludes external baseline metrics, yet SC-005 requires measuring 'total compute time and peak memory usage of the entire experiment' against CI limits. By excluding the external baseline (which runs on larger resources), the task fails to capture the full resource profile required to validate the 'deployment feasibility' claim in SC-005, effectively dropping the acceptance criterion for the baseline's resource contribution.

T029a requires imputing failed baseline 'time_to_pivot' with a 'fixed timeout value' from config.py. However, config.py (T007) defines TIMEOUT_SECONDS for the *rule engine* (CI limit), not the external baseline which runs on different hardware. Using the CI timeout as a proxy for the baseline's failure time violates the semantic integrity of the 'Time-to-Pivot' metric for the baseline, weakening the statistical comparison required by SC-001.

T019a mandates a stratified sample of 'exactly 100' tasks. If any stratum has fewer than the required sample size, the task fails. This introduces a hard constraint not present in the Spec (which says 'stratified random sample of 100 unseen tasks' without specifying failure conditions for small strata). This silently narrows the acceptance criteria, potentially blocking the experiment if the dataset distribution is skewed, violating the 'no retroactive narrowing' principle.
